new_statements.rule_in_words: Second-hand areal generalisation: in the languages of the interior/centre of (south) Malakula there is a strong accent on the penultimate syllable and the final vowel is heavily reduced. Not stated for Dixon Reef/Aveteian specifically; whether Aveteian (spoken north of the Ninde area, west Malakula) falls under 'the center of the island' is not said.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Separately, Tryon 1976:47 (POC vowel correspondences, row 111 Dixon Reef) gives *u > ə 'In unstressed position' (fn.5), implying stressed/unstressed alternation in the Dixon Reef I data, but without saying where stress falls.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level ('next to last syllable'), from transcription practice in Charpentier's wordlists; areal statement covering the Lendamboi/Small Nambas interior languages, quoted by the survey in the Lendamboi section, not in the Aveteian entry. Lynch & Crowley add that the phonemic status of the reduced final vowels is unclear.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog dixo1238 'Dixon Reef' (ISO dix) = Aveteian (Charpentier 1982a:45 [avəteiana]; François et al. 2015 table row 101). 'Dixon Reef' (Tavendrua) is a coastal village where speakers of several interior languages now live; Tryon 1976's list 111 'Dixon Reef I' (G.J. Fox) is what Lynch & Crowley 2001:84 tentatively identify as Aveteian, while Tryon's 'Dixon Reef II (Ma)' (list 111a, Charpentier) is Nasarian [nvh], and the language currently used in Dixon Reef village is Lendamboi/Letemboi (Lynch & Crowley 2001:72). The quoted stress remark is an areal statement about 'the languages of the center of the island' (interior south Malakula), not about Aveteian in particular.

sources.note: Survey, no phonology of Dixon Reef/Aveteian. p.71 fn.6 (in §3.7.1 Lendamboi) quotes Charpentier 1982a:63: in 'the languages of the center of the island, there is a strong tonic accent on the next to last syllable, and the final vowel is so destressed as to become almost unrecognizeable' — an areal remark, not tied to Aveteian. §3.7.25(2) Aveteian p.84: possibly extinct; Charpentier 1982b records nothing of it; Tryon 1976 'Dixon Reef I' list (G.J. Fox) 'may well represent Aveteian'. §3.7.25(1) p.84: Tryon's 'Dixon Reef II' list = Nasarian.
